successors.note: Sold on 1 November 1346: 'In 1346, Estonia (Harria and Vironia) was sold for 19,000 Cologne marks to the Teutonic Order'; Narva went in 1345. The Cliopatria Teutonic Order dossier files the Estonia gain under the counterpart danish-magnates.

capitals.name: Reval (Tallinn)
capitals.note: Reval was 'founded at Lindanise after the 1219 invasion'; the Danes built the fortress Castrum Danorum on Toompea. The castle passed to the Order in May 1343; the page names no later seat.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row (its Kingdom of Denmark shape may draw the conquest, which the Livonian Brothers dossier shows inside the Danish shape of 1227). June 1219: 'the fleet of Valdemar II landed in the harbor of Lindanise (Tallinn)'; the Battle of Lyndanisse is dated 15 June.

correction.text: Danish Estonia 1220-1226: Harria, Vironia and Jerwia in northern Estonia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page does not date the conquest of Harria, Vironia and Jerwia; by 1227 'the Livonian Brothers of the Sword conquered all Danish territories in northern Estonia', and in 1238 Harria and Vironia returned while Jerwia stayed with the Order, so all three were Danish before 1227. 1220 is the year Denmark gave up Sakala and Ugaunia and the first Duke of Estonia was appointed. The shape is county names; no area is on the page.

ledger.note: 15 June 1219: Valdemar II's fleet lands at Lindanise and wins the Battle of Lyndanisse; Reval is founded. 'In 1219, the fleet of Valdemar II landed in the harbor of Lindanise (Tallinn)' in northern Estonia.

region.text: Danish Estonia 1220-1226: Harria, Vironia and Jerwia in northern Estonia

ledger.note: 1220: northern Estonia is Danish. The page dates only the landing (1219), Denmark's 1220 renunciation of Sakala and Ugaunia and the first Duke of Estonia; that Harria, Vironia and Jerwia were Danish by 1227 follows from its 1227 and 1238 sentences, so the year is a bridging reading.

region.text: Danish Estonia 1220-1226: Harria, Vironia and Jerwia in northern Estonia

ledger.note: 1227: the Brothers of the Sword take the Danish north. 'In 1227, the Livonian Brothers of the Sword conquered all Danish territories in northern Estonia.'

region.text: the Duchy of Estonia of 1238: Harria and Vironia (Jerwia stayed with the Order)

ledger.note: 7 June 1238: the Treaty of Stensby returns Harria and Vironia to Denmark. 'On 7 June 1238 the Teutonic Order concluded the Treaty of Stensby at a royal fortress in the south of Zealand'; 'Harria and Vironia returned to Danish direct rule as the Duchy of Estonia, while Jerwia stayed with the Order.'

region.text: Reval (Tallinn) and Wesenberg (Rakvere), the castles handed to the Order in May 1343

ledger.note: 23 April / 16 May 1343: the St George's Night Uprising and the handover of Reval and Wesenberg. The uprising began on 23 April 1343 in Harria and Vironia; after Sõjamäe (14 May) the Danish subjects in Reval put the city and other Danish holdings under Order protection, the Master garrisoning Reval and Wesenberg. The Danish Estonia page: 'The castles in Reval and Wesenberg were handed over to the Order by the pro-German party on 16 May 1343.'

1345: Narva is handed over and receives Lübeck city rights. 'The castle at Narva was handed over, and Narva received Lübeck city rights' (St George's Night Uprising page: 'Denmark also lost Narva in 1345').

wars.name: Estonian Crusade

zones.text: Danish Estonia 1220-1226: Harria, Vironia and Jerwia in northern Estonia

wars.outcome: The Danes won at Lindanise in 1219 and 'the whole of northern Estonia' fell to Danish control (undated, after 1220); a 1223 Estonian uprising took every Christian stronghold but Tallinn; in 1227 the Livonian Brothers of the Sword conquered all Danish territories in northern Estonia, and the Treaty of Stensby (7 June 1238) returned the Duchy of Estonia to Valdemar II.
wars.note: The page dates the Estonian Crusade's operations from 1208; the Danish phase runs 1219-1227.

wars.name: St. George's Night Uprising

zones.text: Reval (Tallinn) and Wesenberg (Rakvere), the castles handed to the Order in May 1343
the Duchy of Estonia of 1238: Harria and Vironia (Jerwia stayed with the Order)

wars.outcome: The Livonian Master Burchard von Dreileben crushed the rising (Kanavere 11 May, Sõjamäe 14 May 1343) and took Reval and Wesenberg under Order garrison; Harria's last strongholds fell in the winter of 1343 and the Ösel rising ended with a conditional surrender in the winter of 1345; Denmark lost Narva in 1345 and sold Estonia in 1346.
wars.note: The Order's Livonian branch did the fighting; the Teutonic Order in Prussia sent reinforcements. The Livonian Brothers of the Sword had merged into the Teutonic Order in 1237, so only the Livonian branch of the Order is meant.

certainty.note: County names stand in for Harria, Vironia and Jerwia; the page gives no boundary or area. The 1238 line between the Order's Jerwia and Danish Harria is the researcher's reading of the county line.

notes: Type colony: a dependency of the Danish crown (a duchy with a viceroy, first mentioned in 1240). Three pages opened within the 2-5 budget. Not settled: when Harria, Vironia and Jerwia were conquered (the page dates only the 1219 landing), the status of the years 1227-1237 (Danish north Estonia held by the Brothers of the Sword, hence no land), Wiek and Ösel (Danish only in the 1559-1645 period, a different state), the 16 May 1343 handover date (the St George's Night page does not give it; the Danish Estonia page does). The Teutonic Order dossier records the 1346 gain from 'danish-magnates' (a Cliopatria row); the Danish Estonia page and the Teutonic Order are the actual parties. The Estonians who held the land before 1219 are the ancient-estonia dossier. The Livonian Brothers dossier files its 1227 gain from Denmark with a Cliopatria 'Kingdom of Denmark' shape, so the Danish north may be drawn twice in 1219-1227.
